purpose: Quantify the effect of selecting thirty displacement steps after inspecting MOSR results, with emphasis on the real 0.5 um sequences.
primary_population: The same end-frame indices are applied to all methods. Circular-feature candidates must be valid for all five methods and both pillar and via measurements. Line candidates must be valid for all five methods.

selection_rules.acquisition_spread30: Thirty steps spread through acquisition order; does not inspect reconstructed results or nominal error.
selection_rules.timestamp_qc_spread30: Reject adjacent captures separated by more than 30 seconds as acquisition interruptions, then spread thirty steps through the remaining acquisition order. The rule does not inspect any reconstruction output.
selection_rules.time_regular30: Thirty steps whose acquisition gap is closest to the within-sequence median; does not inspect reconstructed results.
selection_rules.existing_formal_common: The thesis's existing Raw-motion-ranked choices, restricted to strict common-valid steps. This may contain fewer than thirty steps after the common-valid restriction.
selection_rules.mosr_internal30: Thirty steps with the lowest MOSR internal feature-to-feature spread. This is method-dependent outcome selection.
selection_rules.mosr_nominal30: Thirty steps with the lowest MOSR error relative to commanded displacement. This is an oracle upper bound and is not a fair primary evaluation.

reference_limit: Absolute error is calculated against nominal commanded motion because the current mapping tables do not contain per-frame numeric PI feedback.
paired_uncertainty: Paired MOSR-minus-baseline advantages use 10000 fixed-seed bootstrap resamples of the same selected method-common observations. Positive advantage means lower MOSR error or spread.
thesis_recommendation: Use timestamp_qc_spread30, or replace it with a predeclared numeric PI-feedback quality rule when the feedback log is recovered. MOSR-dependent selections may be reported only as exploratory sensitivity or upper-bound results.
